entities.summary: Marcus Appuleius was a prominent Roman nobleman and the nephew of Emperor Augustus, serving as Roman consul in 20 BC alongside Publius Silius Nerva. He played a key role in the Roman Senate, which governed the Roman Empire from 27 BC to 284 AD. Appuleius was also known for his military service and participated in the Roman civil war of 20 BC, leading to the death of his uncle and the rise of Tiberius to the throne. His legacy continued to shape Roman politics and society for generations to come. The Roman historian Tacitus described Appuleius as a 'man of great character and integrity,' highlighting his commitment to the Roman Republic and its values. Through his relationships with powerful Roman leaders, Appuleius played a significant role in the tumultuous years following the death of Augustus and the ascension of Tiberius to the throne. As a prominent figure in Roman society, Appuleius left a lasting impact on the course of Roman history, cementing his place as a notable historical figure.
